article_sentences: A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant, while declining to entertain the plea filed by advocate Ujjawal Gaur, directed the registry to forward a copy of the petition to all the respondent authorities, asking them to look into the issues raised and take appropriate remedial measures.

New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Monday refused to entertain a public interest litigation (PIL) seeking directions to ensure effective measures to prevent recurring floods, riverbank erosion and drainage-related problems in Assam and the Brahmaputra Valley.
Appearing in person, Gaur submitted that the administrative lapses highlighted in the petition were amenable to judicial scrutiny and urged the apex court to issue notice to the authorities.

However, the CJI Kant-led Bench observed that the various suggestions and deficiencies highlighted by the petitioner ought to draw the attention of the concerned authorities, but the issue was "not essentially legal" in nature.
Declining to entertain the PIL, the top court directed its registry to forward the petition to all the respondents, who would look into its contents and take appropriate remedial measures.

The plea had sought judicial intervention to ensure effective implementation of the statutory framework governing flood and erosion management and had proposed, among other measures, a high-level expert mechanism to examine the recurring problems.

The petitioner had contended that the recurring devastation caused by floods could not be treated as wholly inevitable when statutory frameworks and specialised institutions had been created for flood control, bank erosion and drainage management.

The plea referred to the Brahmaputra Board Act, 1980, the Assam Embankment and Drainage Act, 1953 and the River Boards Act, 1956, arguing that these laws contemplated scientific investigation, integrated river-basin planning and implementation of measures relating to floods, erosion and drainage.

It relied on successive reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) which, according to the petitioner, had recorded deficiencies in flood-control planning, execution and maintenance, drainage management, floodplain management and monitoring of projects.

The petition specifically referred to the CAG's Performance Audit on "Flood Control in Assam", contained in Report No. 5 of 2018, which, it claimed, identified deficiencies in integrated basin-wise planning, floodplain zoning, hydrological and morphological studies, execution and monitoring of flood-control works.

It also relied on official records concerning drainage congestion, backflow, inadequate drainage through sluices, encroachment upon natural drainage channels, sedimentation and river morphology as factors aggravating flood vulnerability.

The petitioner further highlighted a shortage of technical manpower in the Brahmaputra Board, referring to an official Lok Sabha reply dated December 12, 2024, which disclosed that 65 of its 182 sanctioned technical posts remained vacant in 2024.

stories.headline: Did SIR deletions change Tamil Nadu assembly election’s outcome?
stories.title: Did SIR deletions change Tamil Nadu assembly election’s outcome?
stories.summary: While a businessline analysis reveals a striking geographical overlap between high voter removals and TVK victories, experts urge caution against reading it as a conspiracy
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) have stirred protests not just at the national but at the State level too.
In Tamil Nadu, DMK president and former Chief Minister MK Stalin has recently said that the deletion of several lakh voters was one of the reasons for his party’s loss.
The social media is abuzz about how TVK victory may have been aided by these deletions.
A businessline analysis of the granular data on SIR deletions and the outcome of the TN assembly elections in 2026, throws us some interesting trends.
TVK has struggled to win in constituencies where the SIR deletions were lower but has recorded more wins in constituencies where the deletions were higher.
Political analysts and experts however warn that not much should be read into these numbers.
We compared the net reduction in voter count in each constituency as per the April 2026 electoral roll with pre-SIR numbers.
Of the total 234 constituencies, 19 constituencies had lower deletions, of up to 10,000 voters.
In these, the TVK won 2 seats, the DMK 7, the AIADMK 6 and others 4.
Eighty constituencies had deletions between 10,000 to 20,000 voters.
The TVK won 22 of these constituencies, the DMK 20, the AIADMK 24 and others 14.
Sixty-six constituencies had deletions between 20,000 to 30,000.

stories.headline: Madras High Court begins hearing Tamil Nadu CM Vijay’s plea to reject election petitions
stories.title: Madras High Court begins hearing Tamil Nadu CM Vijay’s plea to reject election petitions
stories.summary: Justice V. Lakshminarayanan accepts a request made by senior counsel Srinath Sridevan to hear the four applications one after the other
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Madras High Court on Monday (October 5, 2026) commenced hearing arguments on an application filed by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to reject an election petition filed by a voter, S. Dinesh, challenging his victory from the Perambur Assembly constituency this year.

Justice V. Lakshminarayanan is seized of three election petitions, including the one filed by another voter, T.N. Lakshmi Narasimhan, and Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam’s losing candidate R.D. Shekar, filed against the Chief Minister’s victory in Perambur by a margin of 53,715 votes.

Apart from these three, one more election petition had been filed by DMK candidate S. Inigo Irudayaraj, challenging Mr. Vijay’s victory from the Tiruchi East Assembly constituency, which he had vacated after contesting and winning from both constituencies.

The judge accepted a request made by senior counsel Srinath Sridevan, representing the Chief Minister, to hear the arguments one after another on the applications filed for rejecting each of the four election petitions, as there were certain differences in each case despite overlapping pleadings.

He began hearing the plea to reject Mr. Dinesh’s election petition – filed through the latter’s counsel V.R. Shanmuganathan – first, and decided to take up the application to reject Mr. Narasimhan’s election petition thereafter, since they got numbered one after another.

Senior counsel Gopal Sankaranarayanan, assisted by Pranjal Agarwal and Dixita Gohil, commenced his arguments to reject the first election petition and contended that there was no basis for the allegation of the Chief Minister not having made full and proper disclosure of his assets and liabilities.

He took the court through the evolution of the legal requirement of candidates disclosing their assets, beginning from the 170th Law Commission report submitted in 1999, which recommended such a measure for the first time and also a catena of judgments that were delivered on the issue thereafter.

However, since Mr. Sankaranarayanan could not conclude his arguments on Monday and sought time to continue his submissions some other day, the judge decided to hear him on Tuesday as well, before granting an opportunity to the election petitioner’s counsel Mr. Shanmuganathan to respond.

stories.headline: Odisha government announces to hold student union election after a gap of eight years
stories.title: Odisha government announces to hold student union election after a gap of eight years
stories.summary: Process of elections to be completed in next 10 days; will begin from October 7 and come to end on October 16, 2026
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Odisha government on Monday (Octobeer 5, 2026) announced that student union elections will be held on higher education campuses after a gap of eight years.
The elections will be completed within the next 10 days.
Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi approved conducting student union elections, which involves massive security arrangement in view of possible violence on campuses.

Speaking after his meeting with the Odisha Chief Minister, State Higher Education Minister Suryabanshi Suraj said, “the detailed timeline and complete information will be provided by the department very soon.
A final decision has been taken to hold the elections before the Dussehra holidays, and colleges will issue their own notifications on the October 7, 2026.
Nominations will be filed on the October 9, and the elections will be held on the October 15 and the oath-taking ceremony will be held on the morning of October 16.”
“We believe that conducting these elections is important because today’s students and student leaders are the future leaders of Odisha.

This process will help them understand democratic responsibilities, the importance of democracy, and constitutional values, preparing them to take up leadership roles in the future,” said Mr. Suryabanshi.
Stating that the this is a significant step, the Minister informed “student union elections had been suspended since 2017.
We had also promised in our election manifesto that these elections would be conducted.
After formation of our government in 2024, we spent 2025 addressing various issues on campuses, and in 2026 we are now moving ahead with student union elections.”
He said to ensure peaceful and orderly elections, the Supreme Court’s 2005 verdict and the recommendations of the J. M Lyngdoh Committee, which were followed earlier, will continue to be implemented.

stories.headline: Flydubai co-pilot allegedly plotted Ben Gurion crash in terror-style attack
stories.title: flydubai co-pilot allegedly plotted Ben Gurion crash in terror-style attack
stories.summary: Jerusalem, Oct 5 : The Omani co-pilot who attempted to crash a flydubai flight bound for Tel Aviv had planned to deliberately crash the aircraft into a building or another plane at Israel's Ben Gurion Airport, according to reports in the Israeli media. Hamam Al-Hammami, an Omani first officer who is currently under arrest, reportedly told investigators in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) that he intended to continue operating flydubai Flight 1073 normally after killing the aircraft's captain, Indian pilot Smit Machchhar. According to the reports, his plan was to obtain the necessary landing clearances without arousing suspicion and then crash the aircraft into a building or another jet at the airport in an attack resembling the September 11, 2001, attacks. Quoting sources, Ynet reported that Al-Hammami told investigators that he intended to initiate the plan while the aircraft was over Jordan and approaching Israel. By waiting until the final stage of the flight, he believed that he would prevent anyone from understanding what was happening in time to alert authorities or stop him from carrying out the plan. The reports further said that Al-Hammami had also told investigators that if he was unable to crash the aircraft at Ben Gurion Airport, he planned to target a skyscraper in Tel Aviv or one of the US military bases in Jordan. However, the plan was thwarted after Captain Machchhar, despite suffering serious injuries, fought back against the co-pilot. The Indian pilot managed to send distress signals and open the cockpit door, enabling crew members and passengers to intervene and restrain Al-Hammami. Two off-duty pilots travelling on the aircraft subsequently helped regain control of the plane and safely landed it in Saudi Arabia, preventing the attack from being carried out. Captain Machchhar, who is currently receiving treatment at a hospital in Abu Dhabi, recounted the attack during a conversation with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday. He said that Al-Hammami had asked to pray shortly before attacking him with a crash axe. Machchhar recalled that the first blow landed heavily on his head and that he initially believed the aircraft itself had suffered some kind of impact. At first, Captain Machchhar said he thought the plane had been hit. However, as the assault continued, he realised that the danger was coming from the person sitting beside him in the cockpit. "The blows kept coming. I realised that it's not the aircraft; it's the other guy who was in the cockpit with me," Machchhar said. Sources cited by Israel's Channel 12 reportedly said that Al-Hammami had initially intended to carry out the plan in July but postponed the operation at the last moment because he was friends with one of the crew members. Reports also stated that Al-Hammami had flown to Ben Gurion Airport several times in the months before the incident after joining flydubai. According to the reports, he told investigators that during a visit to Israel in June, he concentrated on gathering information and preparing for the alleged attack. A Channel 13 report said that the Omani co-pilot had planned the attack even before joining flydubai, the low-cost Emirati airline that operates flights between Israel and the UAE. "I looked into which airline flies to Tel Aviv. That's why I chose flydubai. I planned it even before I was accepted," he reportedly told investigators. The Italian newspaper Corriere della Sera reported that after attacking Captain Machchhar, Al-Hammami switched off the aircraft's engines and pushed the rudders forward. According to the report, the actions caused the aircraft to lose around 16,000 feet of altitude in less than a minute, bringing it close to the speed of sound. As the investigation into the flydubai incident continues, preliminary details have also raised questions about possible security lapses and the process through which the co-pilot was cleared to operate the flight. Officials have already said that Al-Hammami's own country had previously barred him from flying because of concerns related to his alleged extremist views. Questions have also been raised over how an Omani citizen, from an Arab country that does not have diplomatic relations with Israel, was permitted to operate a flight carrying Israeli passengers to Tel Aviv. Al-Hammami, 29, is an Omani citizen whose father is Omani and mother Syrian. He had lived in Syria during the country's civil war and had reportedly posted messages online expressing support for al-Qaeda. It also remains unclear how flydubai failed to identify Al-Hammami as a potential security concern before allowing him to serve as a co-pilot on flights to Israel. Regional officials told the Associated Press that Emirati authorities had shared information concerning passengers and crew members, including their nationalities. However, the officials said that Israel had not raised any red flags concerning either passengers or members of the crew. The officials spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to publicly discuss details of the ongoing investigation. Israel's domestic security agency, Shin Bet, said that the Transportation Ministry is responsible for vetting passenger lists received from foreign flights. Transportation Minister Miri Regev, in a post on X, said that responsibility for flight security lies with the security agencies and that her ministry had not been provided with a passenger list or received any warnings concerning the flight. Sharing passenger and crew information is considered a standard aviation procedure. However, Dvir Rubenstien, head of aviation security at Israel's Transportation Ministry, told Army Radio that the ministry relies on security checks carried out locally and does not possess the tools or capacity to independently conduct checks on every passenger travelling on every flight. --IANS

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday agreed to fast-track a nearly four-decade-old compensation dispute arising from the 1988 Ahmedabad air crash that killed 133 people, after Air India sought an urgent hearing in a case that could potentially reshape how compensation is calculated in air-crash claims.
A bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant agreed to list the matter before Justices Aravind Kumar and N.V. Anjaria, who had earlier heard the long-running dispute.
“List before the bench presided by Justice Aravind Kumar,” the CJI said.
Mint reported earlier on Monday that Air India had sought an early hearing of the case, which was last heard in December 2025 but was not taken up thereafter.
The airline subsequently moved an application seeking an early hearing.

At the heart of the dispute is a question that has remained unresolved for decades: should compensation for victims of an air crash be calculated using principles developed by the Supreme Court for road accidents under the Motor Vehicles Act, or should aviation accidents be governed by a separate framework?
Written submissions filed by victims’ families and reviewed by Mint argue that Motor Vehicles Act principles should not automatically apply to air crashes.
The claimants contend that passengers have little or no control over the operation, maintenance or safety of an aircraft and generally have no knowledge of its technical functioning.
They argue that compensation should instead be determined under ordinary principles of tort law, with victims receiving full or just compensation.

The submissions also seek consideration of factors such as actual income, future earning capacity and changes in earnings over time, rather than relying solely on standardised formulas developed for road accidents.

The Supreme Court’s decision to hear the matter comes against the backdrop of last year’s Air India crash that killed 260 people, with several pleas concerning air safety and the crash investigation pending before the court.

stories.title: Supreme Court asks High Court to consider plea against Centre’s decision to take over Delhi Gymkhana Club
stories.summary: The Court permitted 11 club members to move the Delhi High Court, after the High Court had earlier refused their plea on the ground that only the club could challenge the Centre’s decision
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday (October 5, 2026) asked the Delhi High Court to consider a plea by 11 members of the Delhi Gymkhana Club, who had challenged the Centre's decision to take over the club's 27.3-acre premises and the subsequent eviction proceedings.

A Bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana was told by senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for the members, that the Delhi High Court had refused to entertain their plea on the ground that only the club could challenge the Centre's decision.
Mr. Singh said the High Court had asked the members to get a clarification from the Supreme Court that they could also move the plea there.
The Court permitted them to move the High Court, subject to objections that may be raised by the other side regarding maintainability and other legal oppositions.

Mr. Singh, appearing for the 11 members, had earlier told the Bench that a Central government-nominated committee was presently managing the club, and that it could not fight a legal battle with the government.

On September 3, 2026, the Centre, in a separate case, told the Delhi High Court that it would not take any coercive action until September 16, 2026, against the club in relation to its eviction from the premises on Safdarjung Road.

The High Court was hearing pleas by club member Vijay Khurana and others, seeking a stay on the June 29, 2026, show-cause notice for eviction issued to the club's management by an estate officer of the Land and Development Office (L&DO).

Vipin Aggarwal and ten other club members, in their petition filed through lawyer Nitin Saluja, sought the quashing of the resumption notification issued by the L&DO on May 22, 2026, and the show-cause notice issued by the estate officer on June 29, 2026.

stories.headline: RBI expected to raise Repo Rate to 5.50%; what it means for loan EMIs
stories.title: RBI expected to raise Repo Rate to 5.50%; what it means for loan EMIs
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'repo rate' in title weight 42
article_sentences: With inflation firming and global central banks tightening, the RBI’s Monetary Policy Committee is widely expected to end its extended pause and raise the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%.
The move, if announced, would be India’s first rate hike since February 2023—and could gradually push up EMIs on home, auto and business loans.
The Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is meeting at a delicate moment, with domestic inflation ticking upward even as major global central banks tighten policy aggressively.

Market participants and economists increasingly expect the RBI to begin a shallow tightening cycle with a measured 25-basis-point increase in the repo rate, taking it from 5.25 per cent to 5.50 per cent.
The six-member MPC began its October review on Monday and is scheduled to announce its decision on October 7.
A 25-bps move, if announced, would be the first repo-rate increase since February 2023, after the central bank held the rate unchanged through four consecutive policy reviews in 2026.
The policy dilemma has sharpened against a backdrop of aggressive rate increases by the US Federal Reserve and the Bank of Japan to combat persistent inflation.
However, Ajitabh Bharti, Executive Director and Co-founder of CapitalXB, argues that India’s macroeconomic position gives the RBI more room for calibration than many of its global peers.
“India cannot pursue a one-to-one alignment with global rate trajectories.
The RBI must balance currency stability and internal liquidity management without over-tightening into a still-moderate inflation environment,” Bharti said.
He pointed out that headline inflation averaged just 1.9 per cent between April 2025 and February 2026, well below the RBI’s 4 per cent medium-term target.

While inflation has risen more recently -- retail inflation rose to 4.82 per cent in August, remaining above target for a third consecutive month -- the broader price environment remains comparatively contained.
